observations: The page number «92» stands at the head of the page, centred, with a rule below it. The page has no signature. L01: «Ekliptik ist).» completes the sentence that ends p. 91 (JP2 0123, L38), «wenn Z der Zenit und P der Pol der».

L01-L08: al-Battānī's parallax of altitude in the circle Z A of the figure of p. 91, resolved by the sines of the angles of longitude and latitude. L14-L29: al-Khwārizmī's Table 77: its first column is the hour angle of the moon for the parallax in longitude and its ecliptic zenith distance, at the culmination of the point of the ecliptic, for the parallax in latitude; to be compared with the table.

L30-L41. Checked: the true conjunction of 23 January 901, 6h 44m 29s in the morning at Cordova (p. 83, JP2 0115), with the true longitude of the sun and the moon 303° 19′ 48″ and an obliquity of 23° 51′: the right ascension of the sun is 305° 43′, the hour angle −78° 53′, the right ascension of the midheaven 226° 50′; the ascendant comes out at 297° 33′, 297° 16′ and 296° 48′ for latitudes of 37° 30′, 37° 53′ (Cordova) and 38° 30′, so that Suter's 297° 3′ answers to a latitude of about 38° 10′. The point of the ecliptic in the midheaven is then 229° 23′. The sun, about a quarter of an hour before its rising, stands about 6° after the ascendant.

L23: «zo bezeichnen»; see the critical note. L41: a dark mark above the u of «subtrahieren», not an umlaut; not transcribed. L39: «Aszensional-Differenz», with sz, where pp. 73-75 (JP2 0105-0107) have «Ascensional-Differenz»; as printed. L33: «29. Muḥarram» upright, with the dot under the ḥ; L34: «18h 44m 29s», the letters raised.
The dashes: L01 «93—94», L32 «82—84», N01 «285—295», the long dash set close; L28 «ist. — In», the long dash with a space on either side.

Spaced type, marked {sp:}: «Batt.», «Kh.», «Burgess», «Nallino»; italics: «ZA», «Parallaxe», «Länge», «Breite» (L05, L19, L24), «Sūrya-Siddhānta», «Meridiandistanz», «Ekliptik-Zenitdistanz», «Funktion», «Stundenwinkels,», «Zenitdistanz.», «Stundenwinkel», «Medium Coelum», «Aszendenten», «Horoscopus», «Beispiel», «Konjunktion», «Transl.».
The colons and semicolons stand after the thin space of the edition (8-12 px measured).
The list of misprints, p. [237] (JP2 0271, L15), reads «so» for «zo» in L22, the 19th line from the foot of the text (critical note AK07-CN072).
